I will make a total sweater and then introduce what the workflow is like. After that, I'll take you to look at the effect of our sweater. ### Types of Sweater Construction Our sweater is divided into four types: 1. **Cut and Sew**: This is our cutting and sewing together. It’s one of the three main ways of making clothes. 2. **Sewing Each Fabric Piece Separately**: After it's done, it needs to be sewn together without cutting. 3. **Sewing the Pattern with Fabric**: Similar to the second method, but the pattern is sewn together with the fabric. 4. **One-Piece Shape**: This method involves no process of matching; everything is sewn together. All four ways are made in 3D in the first method. We can use this 3D representation to showcase some details of our sweater, such as the collection of flowers, the 3D organization, and the characteristics of our gauze line. We can use them to express the design of our sweater. ## Workflow of Sweater Production Now let's take a look at the workflow of our sweater. You can see that there are three parts here: 1. **Digitalization**: This means we need to use design software to create our DXF paper pattern or make a pattern out of a board. In CLO, you need a board to make our 3D clothing. 2. **Physicalization**: This means that we scan our image. If you don't have this paper pattern, you can scan a real paper pattern. In CLO, we can use the paper pattern we obtain to create some details. 3. **Physical Processing**: We will talk about these three parts one by one. ### Paper Sample Preparation For our paper sample, there are four ways to prepare: 1. **Using 2D or CAD Software**: Create our paper sample using design software. 2. **Adjusting a DXF Paper Sample**: You can also take some of your existing basic paper samples and do some design adjustments. 3. **Directly Drawing in CLO**: Draw our paper sample in CLO according to the size of the supply unit. 4. **Collating Paper Samples**: You can have a paper sample and insert it into CLO to collate. ### Software and Basic Model Next, let's come to our software. Open one of our basic models of 3D clothing. My first clothing today is to use this basic model to make a change and design my sweater. First, I got this basic model, but I think it's a little bit smaller in size. ### Adjusting Measurements So my first step is to take this volume of the chest and make it bigger. I align the basic line of the chest with the outer line of the board. After aligning, we cut the inner line to do a cut and sew. After cutting and sewing, we simulate. ## Design Adjustments In the 3D window, we can find our shrink line tool. This tool allows direct clothing design in the 3D window. For example, I can adjust the dimensions of the board by pulling it to see the specific adjustment value. To view the one-length of the board, I use the shortcut key Shift + Z. ### Shrinkage and Length Adjustments After showing the length, we can go back to shrink and adjust the length of the board. I want to shrink it to a value of 25, which is 2.5 centimeters. After shrinking, I want to adjust the length of the board. ### Neckline and Sleeve Adjustments Now I'm going to change the shape of the neck. First, I’ll delete the small collar on this top board. Then, using the edge shape line tool, I select the neck point and drag it while referring to the values on the 2D board. After making this change, the sleeve is now a little thinner than my design. I’ll make it a bit fatter by using the same method as the breast circumference treatment from earlier. ## Collar and Gusset Adjustments After making these changes, let's take care of the collar. The collar is also part of our gusset. We use the lift tool to create the collar of the gusset. The shortcut key for the lift tool is S. I measure the length of our collar. After obtaining this number, I enter a slightly smaller value than this length. The gusset has a tightening effect, so it must be smaller than the original length. ## Finalizing the Design After sewing the gusset collar, we find that it's in a very loose state. We need to adjust it to about 80% of the original length. Once adjusted, we can simulate to see if it meets our expectations. ### Choosing Fabric Properties Next, we will give our sweater physical attributes suitable for application.
